title: Name a remedy the reader can actually reach in the no-registered-worker refusal
action: The cap-time refusal for an unregistered execution worker named `bee state worker add` as its FIX. That verb is control-plane and refuses from inside a granted worktree — which is exactly where every dispatched worker runs and reads this message. So the remedy was unreachable from the place it was read, and --inline-reason became the routine answer instead of the exception. Point the FIX at `bee dispatch prepare --claim`, which is where registration actually rides, say plainly that self-registering is the orchestrator's move from the main checkout, and keep --inline-reason as the honest fallback for a dispatch that genuinely did not claim.
acceptance: The refusal names dispatch prepare --claim, states that state worker add is control-plane and refuses from a worktree, and keeps --inline-reason as the fallback; the cells suite stays green.

trace.outcome: The unregistered-worker refusal now names dispatch prepare --claim, the door registration actually rides on, instead of a control-plane verb that refuses from the worktree reading the message
deviations: Ran inline rather than dispatched: tiny lane, one message string, and the bee-build agent type is no longer available in this session. Kind: hit an unforeseen obstacle.

Found while correcting my own misfiled P2 — I had filed that dispatch never registers a worker; reading prepare.rs:1814 showed it does, but only on the --claim path, so the real defect was the unreachable remedy rather than a missing write. Kind: the plan was wrong about a fact.
